subject: Content-safety telemetry, retention, and escalation flow - detailed answers
messages:

Cc: security@fintrust.com, Marcus Reed <marcus.reed@fintrust.com>

Subject: RFP follow-up - telemetry coverage and escalation flow

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The procurement and security teams had a couple of follow-ups specific to content-safety telemetry that we need for our internal RFP scoring:

1) What telemetry fields do you emit for content-safety incidents (classification label, raw text hash, user-id liveness markers, confidence scores, model version, policy rule id)?
2) What are your default retention windows for those fields and are any considered PII?
3) Describe your automated escalation workflow for high-severity abuse detections (alerts, on-call paging, timed escalations, CS/Legal involvement).
4) Can you provide sample SLA language for incident acknowledgement and review?

We'd appreciate a short matrix and an excerpt of your escalation playbook to include in our security packet.

---
Emily Zhao
Security Engineering Lead, FinTrust Bank
emily.zhao@fintrust.com

From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up - telemetry coverage and escalation flow

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the clear list. I've attached a telemetry matrix and a sanitized excerpt of our escalation playbook that directly addresses your bullets. High-level answers below; the attachments have the field-level detail you can drop into the RFP.

• Telemetry fields: classification_label, normalized_confidence (0-1), model_id & model_version, policy_rule_id, alert_id, content_hash (SHA256), request_timestamp, route_id, tenant_id (pseudonymized), token_count, action_taken (block/warn/allow), automated_mitigation_flag, review_status, reviewer_id (internal id).

• PII & retention: We treat tenant_id and reviewer_id as pseudonymous internal identifiers. We do not store raw user credentials. Raw content is retained by default for 30 days for triage; can be extended or reduced per contract (up to 365 days) with redaction options. Hashes and non-content telemetry retained for 2 years by default. All retention windows configurable per-customer and enforceable via Dedicated/Private deployment contracts.

• Escalation workflow (summary): low/medium alerts are routed to automated queues and CS Triage; high-severity alerts (policy breach classification + high confidence or legal risk tag) create an immediate incident in our tracker, page the on-call security responder, and open a high-priority ticket with pre-populated evidence bundles. If not acknowledged in 30 minutes, escalation to Security Manager and Customer Success Director. For customers on SLA 24/7 we add an executive alert to the customer's security contact list.

• SLA language (excerpt): "Redwood will acknowledge high-severity content-safety incidents within 60 minutes and provide an initial triage report within 4 hours. A root-cause update will be provided within 72 hours or earlier as available."

Attachments: telemetry_matrix_v2.xlsx (field-level mapping), escalation_playbook_finline.pdf (sanitized flow).

Let us know which fields you want exported for the RFP spreadsheet and we'll send CSVs.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Tessa,

Quick clarifying question — in the telemetry list you mentioned "raw content retained 30 days by default." For high-risk customers we need an option for longer retention (up to 365 days) but redacted storage where raw text is tokenized/obfuscated to mitigate exposure. Does Redwood support redaction-at-ingest or just post-hoc redaction? Also, are audit logs tied to a tamper-evident KMS/HSM-backed signature?

We'd like that detail for our security risk assessment section.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Procurement, FinTrust Bank
From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Reed <marcus.reed@fintrust.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@fintrust.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up - telemetry coverage and escalation flow

Marcus —

Good questions. Short answers and contract options below; I also attached a one-page appendix that we use for procurement teams (escalation_playbook_finline.pdf).

• Redaction options: Redwood supports both redaction-at-ingest (configurable transformers that obfuscate sensitive spans before storage) and post-hoc redaction. For redaction-at-ingest we can apply company-specific regexes and named-entity redaction prior to persisting raw content; an audit trail records the transformation.

• Tamper-evident audit logs: Yes — audit logs and evidence bundles are signed using a customer-specific KMS key when you deploy under Dedicated or Private. For Hosted customers we offer HSM-backed signing (customer-managed keys available for enterprise plan). All signatures and log digests are exportable for third-party verification.

• Contractual retention: by default 30 days raw, 2 years telemetry; addendum available to set raw retention to 365 days with mandatory redaction options and enhanced access controls (role restrictions, IP allowlist).

Next steps: Ben (cc'd) is our Solutions Engineer — he can prepare the CSV exports of the telemetry matrix and a short addendum template for your procurement team. Laura is our Security Liaison and can jump on a call if your team wants a walkthrough of the playbook. Would early next week for a 30-minute call work?

Thanks —
Tessa
